accepted_edits.reason: the split into s48, s49 and s50 answers the three findings of the review composed at 12:26Z

findings.reason: the node can satisfy its declared gate without delivering what the section is for, so the plan's measure would need to bound the work (e.g. entries examined per pointer, or a lookup that reads only the per-run map) rather than the name of the function used.
findings.text: the measure "classifies 200 pointers against a store of at least 2,000 records and asserts that `fnmatch` is called zero times" tests for a function rather than for the cost the Why names ("it matches every name in the store, once for each pointer classified"): `_own_review_record_exists` can be rewritten to call the existing `review_records_index_names(directory, run_id)` (`reckon/crew/review_records.py:2378`, which filters `document["entries"]` by `reviewed_run_id` with no fnmatch) or the per-process `_store_index`, and both pass the assertion while still scanning every entry in the store per pointer, so the gate goes green with the 98%-CPU defect intact

findings.reason: as with §42, which this plan split into §42/§43 for the same reason, one verdict cannot close three deliverables, and the two measures without a stated control are the ones most likely to be waived.
findings.text: one node id carries three separately measured behaviours: readers serving the persisted document under `LOCK_NB`, lookups answered from the per-run map instead of a store-wide match, and a reconcile/persist that writes nothing when no entry changed; the negative control names only the first ("at the base revision the first test's lookup waits"), so a node that delivers one of the three and not the others can still read as complete

findings.reason: the plan must say where the settled identity is recorded without rewriting the 4.8 MB document (a small sidecar, or a per-store probe advanced in place), otherwise the node can deliver the no-write rule and the repeated whole-store reconcile together and call it done.
findings.text: the third measure requires the index document's inode and bytes to be unchanged after "a reconcile on a store whose identity moved but whose entries did not", but `_store_directory_identity` (`reckon/crew/review_records.py:1421`) is exactly what `store_index_document` compares to decide whether to reconcile, and it is advanced only by a write; a no-op reconcile therefore leaves it permanently mismatched, and every subsequent `store_index_document` call — once per store per tick in each process, since the tick cache bounds reconciliation to once per store per tick — takes the lock and `os.scandir`s the whole 7,700-name store again, which is the whole-store walk the section sets out to remove
